raw_response:
I've been farming these 57 mu for 20 years. Never went to school, but I know my land. Every field, I can tell you what's good and what's bad about it. This year, same as the last few years, I'm putting about 50 mu in spring maize and keeping 7 mu of stevia. The stevia I started a while back — a buyer comes from out of town to collect the dried leaves, so it gives some extra cash. But maize is my real crop, the one that feeds my family.

For the maize, I buy hybrid seed from Old Zhang's shop in the county town. You can't save your own seed from hybrids — I've tried, they grow all strange and thin. Costs about 65 yuan per mu. I hire the tractor man to come plow and plant — 50 mu is too much for my family to do by hand, and I don't own a big tractor myself. When he plants, I put down one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu. That's what I've always done. When the corn gets to knee-height, around June, I topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. Two years ago my neighbor Li tried to save money by skipping the topdress, and his corn turned yellow and gave him two big bags less per mu. I'm not making that mistake. Better to spend the money than lose the yield.

Water — I have my own well, but pumping costs electricity. For maize I irrigate twice: once after planting if the rain doesn't come within a week, and once when the tassels come out. My father always said corn doesn't like wet feet, and twice is enough unless it's a very dry year. For the stevia, that plant is pickier — it needs water. I give it three times, especially before each picking.

I spray herbicide on the maize once, right after planting, to keep the weeds down. If I see armyworms or other bugs later in the summer, I'll spray. But I don't spray for nothing — chemicals cost money and I don't want to waste it.

The stevia is already there from last year, it comes back in April. I give it some fertilizer in spring and again in summer, and weed it by hand between the rows. The hard part is the picking — three times, July, September, and before frost in October. That's when I need hired hands the most. My wife works the stevia with me, and my son helps when he's not at his factory job, but for planting the corn and picking everything, I hire people from the village. 57 mu is too much for four people.

Last year my maize gave me about 900 jin per mu. This year looks normal so far, so I expect about the same. I'm not changing anything. The weather looks right, the soil is the same, and I have enough money for the inputs. If it ain't broke, don't fix it.
